subject: Load scenario matrix and acceptance runbook for Ledgerly onboarding
messages:
From: Irene Choi <irene.choi@redwoodhq.com>
To: Sophie Li <sophie.li@ledgerly.com>, Ledgerly Technical Ops <ops@ledgerly.com>
Cc: Monica Patel <monica_patel@redwoodhq.com>, Ben Carter <ben_carter@redwoodhq.com>
Date: 2026-10-01 09:12 -0700
Subject: Load scenario matrix and acceptance runbook for Ledgerly onboarding

Hi Sophie / Ledgerly team,

Per our onboarding kickoff, I'm sharing a proposed load-scenario matrix and a lightweight runbook so we can align on acceptance criteria before we start runs in staging. Please review the attached CSV — it contains the traffic mixes we recommend (interactive chat, bulk-batch embedding, and API spike tests) along with request size distributions.

Key acceptance targets we propose for the initial acceptance gate:
- P95 generation latency <= 120 ms (single-region, us-west) at baseline concurrency profile
- Tail latency (P99) <= 500 ms for sustained 5-minute windows
- Sustained throughput (tokens/sec) target: 350k tokens/sec aggregated across two Dedicated nodes (expected ~6k rps for average 60-token requests)
- Error rate < 0.5% (5xx / timeouts) during a 30-minute stability window

We recommend a three-step verification:
1) Canary run (single shard, low traffic) to validate model variant and cache priming
2) Ramp test (gradual increase to target RPS) with KV-cache hot path exercised
3) Soak/stability window (30–60 minutes) to confirm steady-state metrics

Attachments: ledgerly-load-scenarios-v1.csv, redwood-runbook-template.md

Questions for you:
- Are the traffic mixes representative of your expected production traffic?
- Any compliance constraints that require more isolated runs (e.g., different VPC/region)?
- Preferred dates/times (we've got a slot next Tuesday/Wednesday in the early AM PST)

I'll loop Monica (implementation lead) and Ben (inference runtime owner) for technical runbook details. If you want, we can include an optional teleconference during the canary.

Thanks,
Irene Choi
Head of Solutions, Redwood Inference
From: Sophie Li <sophie.li@ledgerly.com>
To: Irene Choi <irene.choi@redwoodhq.com>
Cc: Ledgerly Technical Ops <ops@ledgerly.com>, Monica Patel <monica_patel@redwoodhq.com>
Date: 2026-10-02 11:05 -0700
Subject: Re: Load scenario matrix and acceptance runbook for Ledgerly onboarding

Thanks Irene — this is exactly the level of detail we needed. A few quick notes: 

- Traffic mixes: yes, the CSV looks close. We'll add a small additional bucket for multi-turn system prompts (average 180 tokens) — I'll send an updated sample later today.
- Region: Ledgerly requires data to stay in us-west for this environment. Staging is fine in us-west.
- Ramp window: can we cap the initial ramp at 4k rps instead of 6k so we can sanity-check logging and tracing? If that looks good we can attempt a 6k blast later in the week.

Also: we have one custom transformer in our preprocessing that increases tokenization variance; can you confirm whether the KV cache warm-up strategy will still be effective?

Proposed times: 2026-10-05 08:00 PT for canary (30m) and 2026-10-06 09:00 PT for ramp (60m).

Sophie Li
VP Product, Ledgerly
From: Monica Patel <monica_patel@redwoodhq.com>
To: Sophie Li <sophie.li@ledgerly.com>, Irene Choi <irene.choi@redwoodhq.com>
Cc: Ben Carter <ben_carter@redwoodhq.com>
Date: 2026-10-03 13:42 -0700
Subject: Re: Load scenario matrix and acceptance runbook for Ledgerly onboarding

Sophie — good points. Short answers:

- KV cache warm-up: yes, the warm-up strategy still works with token variance; we'll include prefix-affinity priming in the canary to ensure cache hit rates reach expected levels before ramp. Expect to see >70% cache-hit for repeated session flows after a 10-minute primer.
- Ramp cap: 4k RPS for the first ramp is fine. We'll instrument additional tracing (trace-id passthrough) and collect tokenization deltas to validate the preprocessing impact.

I've attached a short helper script (canary-script.sh) that our infra team runs to prime caches and emit telemetry. Run plan:
- 08:00 PT canary: primer (10m) -> baseline (20m) -> quick health check
- 08:45 PT pause and review telemetry (SLAs: P95 <= 120ms, P99 <= 500ms)
- If green, schedule ramp for 10/06 as proposed.

Action items for Ledgerly: please confirm the staging endpoint (+ any auth headers) and provide a sample of the preprocessing transformer output so we can run tokenization deltas against our model.

Attachments: canary-script.sh

—Monica
Implementation Lead, Redwood Inference
From: Ben Carter <ben_carter@redwoodhq.com>
To: Monica Patel <monica_patel@redwoodhq.com>, Irene Choi <irene.choi@redwoodhq.com>
Cc: Sophie Li <sophie.li@ledgerly.com>
Date: 2026-10-04 09:16 -0700
Subject: Re: Load scenario matrix and acceptance runbook for Ledgerly onboarding

Quick technical notes from runtime: 

- Node sizing: for Ledgerly's profile (avg 60 tokens, multi-turn bursts) our Dedicated 4-GPU profile should comfortably hit 4k RPS with KV cache primed; hitting 6k will require either a second dedicated shard or enabling a higher batch depth. We'll recommend starting with one shard + burst policy.
- Quantization/precision: we can test an int8 profile to reduce memory pressure; expect a ~12–18% throughput uplift at slight quality delta — if Ledgerly wants to evaluate, we'll include quality regression checks in the runbook.
- Telemetry: please ensure sampling includes tokenized-length histograms and per-request trace-id matching so we can correlate tail latency to specific transformer variants.

I've uploaded a short guidance PDF (kv-cache-guidance.pdf) to the Drive folder referenced below.

Ben Carter
Senior Platform Engineer, Redwood Inference
From: Irene Choi <irene.choi@redwoodhq.com>
To: Sophie Li <sophie.li@ledgerly.com>, Ledgerly Technical Ops <ops@ledgerly.com>
Cc: Monica Patel <monica_patel@redwoodhq.com>, Ben Carter <ben_carter@redwoodhq.com>
Date: 2026-10-05 15:28 -0700
Subject: Re: Load scenario matrix and acceptance runbook for Ledgerly onboarding

Thanks all — schedule confirmed for canary on 2026-10-05 08:00 PT (Irene/Monica/Bob from infra will join) and ramp attempt on 2026-10-06 09:00 PT pending canary green. Final acceptance checklist below — please confirm by EOD 10/05: 

Final acceptance checklist (sign-off criteria):
- Canary: primer + 20 min baseline with P95 <= 120ms and error rate < 0.5%
- Ramp: sustain 4k RPS for 15 minutes with P95 <= 140ms (acceptable transient allowance), no more than 1% error rate
- Soak: 30-minute steady-state with P99 <= 500 ms and CPU/GPU utilization within expected ranges documented in runbook
- Artifacts: telemetry dump (CSV), perf traces (zip), runbook versioned in Drive, HubSpot note updated with run outcome

Action items:
- Ledgerly: confirm staging endpoint and provide sample transformer output by 10/04 EOD (Sophie)
- Redwood (Monica/Ben): prepare canary script and telemetry dashboards; attach links to Drive and HubSpot (we added HS-927410 to the deal)
- All: decide whether to include int8 quantization trial during the ramp (Ben suggested this as optional)

Drive folder: https://drive.google.com/drive/folders/1AaBck-ledgerly-onboard
HubSpot record: HS-927410

If Sophie confirms the staging endpoint and sample output, we'll proceed with the primer tomorrow morning.

Best,
Irene Choi
Head of Solutions, Redwood Inference
